normalization_questions_if_source_code_i: Which exact Linear A column/string was consumed by the comparison step?
Was case preserved, lowercased, uppercased, or otherwise normalized?
Were leading/trailing or internal spaces removed or preserved?
Was punctuation removed, preserved, or selectively transformed?
Were vowels deleted before or after any other normalization steps, and was the vowel set exactly a/e/i/o/u in both cases?
What happened when vowel removal produced an empty cluster?
Were duplicate Linear A rows retained?
Was comparison ordinary exact string equality or another equality/collation rule?

suggested_email.subject: Request for the exact study inputs used in Nepal & Perono Cacciafoco (2024) Linear A computational analysis
suggested_email.body:
Dear Professor Perono Cacciafoco,

I am conducting a reproducibility-focused computational audit of the methods reported in Nepal & Perono Cacciafoco (2024), ‘Minoan Cryptanalysis: Computational Approaches to Deciphering Linear A and Assessing Its Connections with Language Families from the Mediterranean and the Black Sea Areas’ (DOI: 10.3390/info15020073). The article's Data Availability Statement notes that the study data can be made available to interested scholars upon request.

To reproduce the raw consonant-cluster comparison faithfully, before any manual plausibility or semantic filtering, I would be very grateful if you could share the exact study inputs used for that paper, if they are still available: (1) the Linear A master-list file used by the comparison program; (2) the exact dictionary/input files used for Ancient Egyptian, Luwian, Hittite, Proto-Celtic and Uralic; (3) the exact Python source/version used for the 2024 run, or alternatively a precise description of the preprocessing steps and a few input/output examples; and (4) if available, the provenance/file connecting the paper's derived phonetic grid to the New Format / Linear A comparison strings. The raw unfiltered program output, if retained, would also be extremely useful as a reproduction check.

My aim is not to reverse-engineer the selected published matches or to make a new decipherment claim, but to preserve the original preprocessing and raw exact-match layer exactly and then test it under pre-registered chance/permutation controls. I will preserve the original files and their provenance and will respect any access or redistribution conditions you specify.

If convenient, the original files as used are preferable to reformatted copies; I can compute cryptographic hashes and technical metadata after receipt.

Thank you very much for your time and for making the methodology and program publicly documented.

Best regards,
Oleksandr Ahapov / Hawkar

upon_receipt_pipeline: Preserve original bytes before opening or converting files.
Compute SHA-256 and byte length for every original file.
Create R3C-3 execution-input receipt under the frozen receipt contract.
Establish normalization contract and canaries before inspecting language score outcomes.
Generate admitted normalized execution views reproducibly.
Run frozen R3C-3 v0.1.2 raw-match and N1/N2 audit without changing languages, metrics, nulls or thresholds.
